questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Soviet System and Its Collapse' refers to.
questions.a: The Soviet system, built after the 1917 Bolshevik revolution, concentrated economic and political power in the communist party and a centrally planned economy; by the 1980s stagnation, shortages and the arms burden with the USA had weakened it, and Gorbachev's reforms of glasnost and perestroika accelerated rather than saved the system.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Soviet System and Its Collapse'.
questions.a: Reform exposed the rot: once censorship and central control loosened, republics and nationalities moved for independence.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Soviet System and Its Collapse' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Soviet System (source: leps101.txt soviet system, stagnation and Gorbachev reforms sections)

concepts.title: Berlin Wall's Fall and Bipolarity's End

questions.q: Using the method 'Berlin Wall's Fall and Bipolarity's End', work with: ussr_end_year = 2600, wall_year = 1989. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of wall_to_end.

Take the relation taught for 'Berlin Wall's Fall and Bipolarity's End' and work with: ussr_end_year = 2600, wall_year = 1989. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of wall_to_end.
Explain in your own words what 'Berlin Wall's Fall and Bipolarity's End' refers to.
questions.a: The Berlin Wall, built at the height of the Cold War as its greatest symbol, was toppled by the people in 1989; two years later the Soviet Union itself dissolved, so the wall's fall and the union's end are separated by the difference of 1991 and 1989.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Berlin Wall's Fall and Bipolarity's End'.
questions.a: Subtracting the wall's fall year from the Soviet end year gives the gap in years between the two events.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Berlin Wall's Fall and Bipolarity's End', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Shock Therapy and Its Consequences' refers to.
questions.a: Post-communist states adopted shock therapy - abrupt transition to capitalism under Washington consensus prescriptions: privatisation of assets, free trade, currency convertibility; the therapy produced deep initial contraction, oligarchic capture of privatised assets and social distress, with uneven recovery across states.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Shock Therapy and Its Consequences'.
questions.a: Speed was the therapy and the disease: overnight privatisation handed state assets to insiders while safety nets vanished.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Shock Therapy and Its Consequences' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Shock Therapy in Post-communist Regimes (source: leps101.txt shock therapy features and consequences sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India and Post-communist States' refers to.
questions.a: India maintained long friendship with the Soviet Union - defence supplies, diplomatic support and trade - and after 1991 rebuilt ties with Russia and the new republics through energy, defence partnership and connectivity initiatives like the International North-South corridor.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and Post-communist States'.
questions.a: The end of bipolarity did not end the partnership: India and Russia re-tooled an old friendship for a multipolar market age.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India and Post-communist States' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: India and Post-communist Countries (source: leps101.txt India-Soviet relations and post-1991 ties sections)
